issue.finding: The proposed finite quotient identifies worlds solely by truth values of variables in A and orders those types by subset. This can add accessibility arrows that were absent in the original model, so it does not preserve implication truth. Counterexample: take two worlds w and u with only identity accessibility, V(p)={u}, V(q)=empty, and A=(p implies q). A is true at w, where no accessible world satisfies p. The quotient has types [w]=empty and [u]={p}; the subset order makes [u] accessible from [w], where p holds and q fails, so A is false at [w]. Thus the displayed satisfaction equivalence and the offered proof of the finite-model theorem are invalid, although this does not refute the theorem itself.

issue.finding: The source attributes a single closest-world iff truth condition to both Stalnaker and Lewis. The source's own closing sentence acknowledges different assumptions and different valid inferences.
issue.action: Identified the Marathi account as a rough sketch and inserted an OLINC-238 reader note explaining the distinction. The original prose's example and symbols remain translated; no new full counterfactual semantics is claimed.
alternatives: Present the single-world condition as the exact shared Lewis-Stalnaker truth condition

issue.review_question: Should the introductory one-world account be explicitly marked as simplified when attributed to Lewis?
issue.verification_source: https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/david-lewis/ and https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/counterfactuals/

issue.uncertainty: A full independent proof of the renaming theorem is not added; the local induction repair follows the stated clean/dirty definition.
alternatives: Choose an arbitrary highest inference and assert it was dirty without proof.
issue.review_question: Should the induction choose the highest dirty inference and use a strict decrease rather than exact decrement?
